newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel ally rejects Fischler criticism on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Waigel ally rejects Fischler criticism on EMU.

text.p: A leading power-broker in Germany's coalition on Tuesday rejected criticism by European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler that Bonn's hardline position on monetary union would isolate Germany from its partners.
Fischler, an Austrian, told Vienna's Kurier daily that Germany's insistence on a tough stability pact to enforce budget discipline could be counter-productive.

But Michael Glos, parliamentary leader of the Christian Social Union (CSU) -- German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Bavaria-based party -- told Fischler to stick to farm policy and keep out of the EMU debate.
"Whoever criticises automatic sanctions for failing to stick to the EMU criteria is undermining the acceptance of monetary union," Glos told a news briefing.
Germany is demanding tough automatic penalties against countries which fail to stick to the strict fiscal targets set in the Maastricht Treaty once monetary union is in place.

But Bonn has little support from EMU partners, with little progress made at a Franco-German summit in Nuremberg on Monday. Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, still hopes for a deal on the pact before a summit in Dublin this week.

The verbal attacks are extremely rare between Germany and Austria -- which has for years pegged its schilling currency to the German mark -- and give some indication over the resistance facing Waigel's tough stability pact proposals in EU states.
"If they (the Germans) remain stubborn, that will be a problem," Fischler told Tuesday's Kurier.

"Germany is gradually becoming isolated with its hardline position," he said, noting that the European Commission did not support automatic sanctions against countries breaching the budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product by 1997. REUTER
